questions.stem: A family member asks a clinician to release separately maintained psychotherapy notes without the patient's authorization. Which HIPAA principle is most accurate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Psychotherapy notes may be disclosed whenever another person requests health information, because they receive the same disclosure treatment as routine records.","B":"Psychotherapy notes may be disclosed freely for treatment purposes, because HIPAA never requires authorization when information is requested by another clinician.","C":"Psychotherapy notes receive special protection, and with limited exceptions HIPAA generally requires patient authorization before they are disclosed in most cases.","D":"Psychotherapy notes fall outside HIPAA because they are kept separately from the medical record, so federal privacy requirements do not apply to their release at all."}}
questions.rationale: HHS explains that psychotherapy notes are specially protected and generally require patient authorization before disclosure, subject to limited exceptions. Option C states that rule. Option A incorrectly treats psychotherapy notes like routine records. Option B incorrectly assumes treatment-purpose disclosure is automatically allowed to another clinician. Option D incorrectly claims that separate storage removes the notes from HIPAA protection.
questions.source_name: HHS — HIPAA Privacy Rule: Psychotherapy Notes
questions.source_detail: HHS explains that separately maintained psychotherapy notes receive special protection and, with limited exceptions, require the patient's authorization before disclosure; currentness was cross-checked against HHS medical-record guidance reviewed May 30, 2025.

questions.stem: An electronic health record fails to display an expected allergy alert during medication ordering. Which organizational response best supports patient safety?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Investigate the clinical decision-support failure and continue systematic testing, monitoring, and improvement of EHR alerts and order-entry safeguards.","B":"Disable all medication alerts permanently after this event, because one missed warning shows that clinical decision support creates more risk than benefit.","C":"Return immediately to paper-only ordering throughout the organization, because an isolated EHR alert failure proves electronic ordering cannot be made safe.","D":"Leave the system unchanged if no second failure occurs, because clinical decision-support tools do not require ongoing monitoring after implementation."}}
questions.rationale: An allergy-alert failure is a patient-safety signal that warrants investigation and ongoing evaluation of the clinical decision-support system. Option A matches ONC SAFER guidance on safe design, implementation, use, and monitoring of CPOE and CDS. Option B overreacts by disabling all alerts rather than correcting the failure. Option C abandons electronic ordering based on a single defect instead of improving the system. Option D ignores the need for ongoing monitoring after implementation.
questions.source_name: ONC — 2025 SAFER Guide: Computerized Provider Order Entry with Decision Support
questions.source_detail: ONC's current SAFER Guides identify recommended practices for the design, implementation, use, testing, and monitoring of orders, alerts, warnings, and clinical decision support; the CPOE guide page was updated April 28, 2026.

questions.stem: A nurse experiences persistent guilt, anxiety, and loss of professional confidence after being involved in a serious medication error. Which concept best describes this response?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A disciplinary finding that establishes professional incompetence, because emotional distress after an adverse event demonstrates inability to practice safely.","B":"The second-victim phenomenon, in which clinicians involved in serious errors or adverse events may experience substantial emotional and professional distress.","C":"A routine performance issue that should be managed without peer or organizational support, because clinician distress does not affect recovery after an error.","D":"A rare response unrelated to patient-safety events, because clinicians generally do not experience anxiety, guilt, or self-doubt after involvement in harm."}}
questions.rationale: AHRQ PSNet describes significant emotional and professional distress after involvement in errors or adverse events as the second-victim phenomenon. Option B fits the nurse's guilt, anxiety, and loss of confidence. Option A turns distress itself into proof of incompetence, which the concept does not support. Option C incorrectly excludes peer and organizational support. Option D incorrectly characterizes this response as rare and unrelated to patient-safety events.
questions.source_name: AHRQ PSNet — Second Victims: Support for Clinicians Involved in Errors and Adverse Events
questions.source_detail: AHRQ PSNet's primer, reviewed in 2025, describes the substantial emotional and professional impact clinicians may experience after errors or adverse events and discusses organizational support for the second-victim phenomenon.

questions.stem: After a wrong-site surgery, a hospital performs a root cause analysis. What is the primary purpose of this process?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Identify the individual closest to the event and assign direct blame, because personal fault is the main target of a root cause analysis after a sentinel event.","B":"Document the event for legal purposes without changing care processes, because root cause analysis is separate from efforts to prevent recurrence.","C":"Determine whether the event can be removed from internal reports, because the main goal is to reduce the number of documented sentinel events.","D":"Identify underlying system and process factors that contributed to the event and develop actions to reduce the risk of a similar event recurring in the future."}}
questions.rationale: Root cause analysis is intended to understand the system and process factors that contributed to a serious event and to guide changes that reduce recurrence. Option D reflects the Joint Commission's current sentinel-event expectations. Option A centers the process on personal blame rather than contributing factors. Option B separates analysis from preventive improvement. Option C treats the process as a reporting-reduction exercise rather than a patient-safety investigation.
questions.source_detail: Current 2026 Joint Commission guidance states that accredited organizations should identify sentinel events, examine root causes and contributing factors, and make improvements to mitigate the risk of recurrence.

questions.stem: A primary care practice adopts a patient-centered medical home model. Which description best reflects this model?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Care is organized mainly around isolated acute visits, with limited responsibility for coordination across clinicians, settings, or periods between appointments.","B":"Care decisions are directed primarily by clinicians without incorporating patient preferences, because standardization takes priority over individualized goals.","C":"Care is comprehensive, patient-centered, coordinated, accessible, and focused on quality and safety, usually through an ongoing team-based primary care approach.","D":"Care is delivered only during inpatient admissions, because the medical-home model is designed for hospital-based management rather than longitudinal primary care."}}
questions.rationale: AHRQ defines the patient-centered medical home as comprehensive, patient-centered, coordinated, accessible, and focused on quality and safety, with team-based care supporting those functions. Option C includes these defining attributes. Option A reduces the model to disconnected episodic care. Option B removes patient preferences from decision-making. Option D incorrectly limits the medical-home model to inpatient care rather than longitudinal primary care.
questions.source_name: AHRQ — Defining the Patient-Centered Medical Home
questions.source_detail: AHRQ defines the medical home through five core functions: comprehensive care, patient-centered care, coordinated care, accessible services, and quality and safety, typically supported by a team-based primary-care model.
